news.headline: Cheesecake Factory Sees Younger Guests Fuel Sales as Flower Child Expansion Nears
news.quote: younger customers, social media engagement and growing off-premise sales are helping drive traffic

touches.claim: North Italia, Flower Child, and Other FRC provide faster revenue growth than the flagship brand, with fiscal 2025 sales increasing 15.5%, 27.8%, and 18.4%, respectively, compared with 1.0% at The Cheesecake Factory.

Management seeks to grow comparable sales by raising average check through biannual menu price updates alongside menu innovation, the Cheesecake Rewards program, and digital and social media engagement.

Sustaining comparable sales growth requires maintaining customer traffic and perceived value amid competition and consumer discretionary spending sensitivity, because menu price increases can reduce traffic or shift mix unfavorably.

Off-premise sales provide a major channel, representing approximately 21% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales in fiscal 2025 and $50.0 (table in thousands) in fiscal 2025 average weekly sales per restaurant.
Expanding newer concepts—North Italia, Flower Child, and Other FRC—carries heightened execution risk, with no assurance of market acceptance or achieving targeted returns on new locations.

news.why: Management commented that younger guests, social media engagement, and off-premise sales are supporting traffic ahead of upcoming Flower Child expansion.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the General section of Item 2 MD&A in [P4].
business_model.claim: The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated owns and operates 384 experiential dining restaurants across the United States and Canada—including 218 The Cheesecake Factory, 53 North Italia, 47 Flower Child, and 60 Other FRC locations—while 35 international The Cheesecake Factory restaurants operate under licensing agreements.
quotes: We currently own and operate 384 restaurants throughout the United States and Canada under brands including The Cheesecake Factory® (218 locations), North Italia® (53 locations), Flower Child® (47 locations) and additional brands within our FRC portfolio (60 locations).
Internationally, 35 The Cheesecake Factory® restaurants operate under licensing agreements.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1 Business in [P1].
business_model.claim: The Cheesecake Factory restaurants serve a fresh-from-scratch menu of approximately 225 items alongside approximately 45 dessert varieties and a full-service bar, with desserts representing approximately 17%, alcoholic beverages 11%, and off-premise sales approximately 21% of the concept's restaurant sales in fiscal 2025.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory menu features approximately 225 items, exclusive of beverage and dessert items and including items presented on supplemental menus, such as our SkinnyLicious® menu that offers innovative items at 590 calories or less.
We offer approximately 45 varieties of proprietary cheesecake and other desserts in our restaurants.
All of our restaurants offer a full-service bar where our entire menu is served.
During fiscal 2025, alcoholic beverage sales represented 11% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales.
Our brand identity and reputation for offering premium desserts results in a significant level of dessert sales, representing approximately 17% of The Cheesecake Factory sales during fiscal 2025.

We offer all items on our menu, except alcoholic beverages where disallowed by regulation, for off-premise consumption, sales of which comprised approximately 21% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales during fiscal 2025.

In contrast to many restaurant chains, substantially all of our menu items, except those desserts produced at our bakery facilities, are prepared from scratch daily at our restaurants with high-quality, fresh ingredients using innovative and proprietary recipes.

business_model.claim: The company distributes off-premise orders via online ordering and a third-party delivery partner, while restaurant customers pay in cash or cash equivalents at the time of sale and purchase gift cards carrying 176,386 (table in USD thousands) in liabilities.
quotes: We work with a third party to provide delivery service from all of our locations and offer online ordering for to-go sales at all of our domestic locations.

Typically, our requirement for working capital has not been significant since our restaurant customers pay for their food and beverage purchases in cash or cash equivalents at the time of sale, and we are able to sell many of our restaurant inventory items before payment is due to the suppliers of such items.
Gift card liabilities | 176,386 | 212,859

business_model.claim: An integrated bakery division produces cheesecakes and other baked products for company restaurants, international licensees, and third-party customers across supermarkets, mass market retailers, club stores, and other food service and retail channels, alongside international and consumer packaged goods royalty streams.
quotes: Our bakery division operates two facilities that produce quality cheesecakes and other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees and third-party bakery customers.

In addition to selling products throughout the world through various distribution channels, including, without limitation, supermarkets, mass market retailers, club stores and various other food service and retail channels, our bakery facilities are the only sources of most of our baked desserts to our restaurants.

Our objective is to drive margin expansion over time by leveraging incremental sales to increase restaurant-level margins at The Cheesecake Factory concept, leveraging our bakery operations, international and consumer packaged goods royalty revenue streams and G&A expense, and optimizing our restaurant portfolio.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Selected Segment Information table and footnotes in [P6].
business_model.claim: The company reports financial results across the following segments: The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, North Italia, Other FRC (all FRC brands except Flower Child), and Other (Flower Child, Grand Lux Cafe, third-party bakery, international and consumer packaged goods businesses, unallocated corporate expenses, and gift card costs).
quotes: The Other FRC segment includes all FRC brands except Flower Child.

The Other segment includes the Flower Child and Grand Lux Cafe concepts, as well as the Company's third-party bakery, international and consumer packaged goods businesses, unallocated corporate expenses and gift card costs.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Selected Segment Information table in [P6].
business_model.claim: In the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026 (table in thousands), The Cheesecake Factory restaurants generated $2,174,323 of the $3,041,906 total revenues and $349,126 of income from operations, compared with $280,912 revenue and $16,791 operating income at North Italia, $298,867 revenue and $6,604 operating income at Other FRC, and $287,804 revenue and $(163,995) operating loss in Other.

Revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and comparable restaurant sales, with the company expecting to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026 and targeting 7% annual unit growth longer-term.
quotes: Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.

The Company continues to expect to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026, including as many as five The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, eight North Italia locations, seven Flower Child locations and as many as six FRC restaurants.

Longer-term, we believe our domestic revenue growth (comprised of our targeted annual unit growth of 7% in aggregate across concepts and comparable sales growth) combined with margin expansion, planned debt repayments and an anticipated capital return program will support our long-term financial objective of 10% to 15% total return to shareholders, on average.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1A Risk Factors in [P2] and Item 2 MD&A in [P4].
business_model.claim: Comparable restaurant sales move with customer traffic and average check, where average check variations are driven by twice-yearly menu price increases and menu mix shifts.
quotes: We strive to increase comparable restaurant sales by improving customer traffic trends and growing average check.
Average check variations are driven by menu price increases and/or changes in menu mix.

We generally update The Cheesecake Factory menus twice a year, and our philosophy is to use price increases to help offset key operating cost increases in a manner that supports both our margin and customer traffic objectives.
We utilize menu price increases in an effort to help offset inflation of key operating costs.

quotes: Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

Continued menu innovation, our rewards program and significant engagement across social media contributed to the impressive sales growth, while year-over-year improvements in labor productivity and food efficiency supported strong profitability.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Unit Economics section of Item 1 Business in [P1].
business_model.claim: The company leases all restaurant locations, incurs average construction costs of approximately $1,100 to $1,200 per interior square foot, and generated approximately $12.4 million in average sales per full-year The Cheesecake Factory restaurant ($1,151 per productive square foot) in fiscal 2025, with new openings typically seeing elevated initial volumes that normalize over the following months.
quotes: We currently lease all of our restaurant locations and utilize capital for leasehold improvements and furnishings, fixtures and equipment to build out our restaurant premises.
Total construction costs to build our restaurant premises average approximately $1,100 to $1,200 per interior square foot.
Average sales per location for The Cheesecake Factory restaurants open for the full year were approximately $12.4 million for fiscal 2025.

Average sales per productive square foot (defined as all interior square footage plus seasonally adjusted exterior patio square footage) for restaurants open for the full year were approximately $1,151 for fiscal 2025.
Our new restaurants have typically opened with initial sales volumes well in excess of their future run-rate levels.

During the three to six months following the opening of new restaurants, customer traffic has generally settled into its normal pattern, resulting in sales volumes that gradually adjust downward to their post-opening run-rate level.

business_model.claim: Labor is the largest operating cost at 1,059,002 (table in USD thousands), or 34.8% of revenues, in the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026, driven by restaurant and bakery staffing, minimum and tip-credit wage mandates, self-insured healthcare claims, and the labor intensity of preparing a complex menu fresh from scratch.
quotes: Increased restaurant labor costs could impact us more than others in our industry because we have a complex menu made fresh from scratch at our restaurants, requiring more labor at each restaurant location than some of our competitors who use processed foods or commissaries to prepare their foods.

Certain state and localities have significantly increased their minimum wage and/or tip credit wage (or have eliminated the tip credit wage), and require significantly more mandated benefits, and other states and localities may also elect to do so.
Our labor expenses include significant costs related to our self-insured health, pharmacy and dental benefit plans.

business_model.claim: Other operating costs and expenses totaled 822,832 (table in USD thousands), or 27.1% of revenues, in the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026, covering occupancy costs (rent, common area expenses, insurance, licenses, taxes, and utilities), supplies, maintenance, credit card fees, marketing and delivery commissions, incentive pay, and bakery overhead.
quotes: Other operating costs and expenses consist of all other restaurant-level operating costs, the major components of which are occupancy expenses (rent, common area expenses, insurance, licenses, taxes and utilities), dining room and to-go supplies, repairs and maintenance, janitorial expenses, credit card processing fees, marketing including delivery commissions, incentive compensation, and bakery production overhead.

business_model.claim: Food and beverage costs were 655,016 (table in USD thousands), or 21.5% of revenues, in the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026, reflecting raw materials across diversified commodity categories—general grocery, dairy, produce, seafood, poultry, meat, and bread—where cost movements in one category can sometimes offset another.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory restaurant menus are among the most diversified in the foodservice industry and, accordingly, are not overly dependent on a few select commodities.
Changes in costs for one commodity sometimes can be offset by cost changes in other commodity categories.
The principal commodity categories for our restaurants include general grocery items, dairy, produce, seafood, poultry, meat and bread.

business_model.claim: Beyond store-level direct costs, the company incurred 196,168 in general and administrative expenses (6.4% of revenues), 86,262 in depreciation and amortization (2.8%), and 23,591 in preopening costs (0.8%) in the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026 (tables in USD thousands), while newly opened restaurants typically experience higher initial food and labor cost ratios until volumes and management stabilize.
quotes: Depreciation and amortization expenses | 29,175 | 2.8% | 27,419 | 3.0% | 86,262 | 2.8% | 80,361 | 2.9%

G&A expenses consist of the restaurant management recruiting and training program, restaurant field supervision, corporate support and bakery administrative organizations, as well as gift card commissions to third-party distributors.
Preopening costs can fluctuate significantly from period to period based on the number, mix and timing of restaurant openings and the specific preopening costs incurred for each restaurant.

Additionally, our new restaurants have typically required a period of time after reaching normal traffic levels to achieve their targeted restaurant-level margins due to actual-to-theoretical food cost inefficiencies and labor productivity inefficiencies commonly associated with new, highly complex restaurants such as ours.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in Item 1A Risk Factors in [P2].
business_model.claim: Because dining out is a discretionary expenditure, customer traffic and average check are sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, consumer confidence, and competition from full-service chains, independent restaurants, fast casual and quick-service operators, grocery stores, and meal kits.
quotes: Dining out is a discretionary expenditure that is influenced by domestic and global economic conditions, including, but not limited to: geopolitical instability, including armed conflicts, supply shortages, interest rates, changes to the terms of international trade agreements, unemployment, significant cost inflation, public health emergencies, consumer confidence, consumer purchasing and saving habits, credit conditions, stock market performance, home values, population growth, household incomes and tax policy.
We compete directly and indirectly for customer traffic with national and regional full-service dining restaurant chains as well as independently owned restaurants.

In addition, we face competition from fast casual and quick service restaurants, grocery stores and meal kits that have increased the quality and variety of their food products in response to consumer demand.

Internationally, 35 The Cheesecake Factory® restaurants operate under licensing agreements.

competitive_position.claim: Management positions The Cheesecake Factory as an upscale casual dining leader based on high unit productivity, with full-year locations averaging approximately $12.4 million in sales and $1,151 per productive square foot in fiscal 2025.
quotes: We believe that we are a leader in upscale casual dining given the historically high average sales per square foot of our restaurants as compared to others in this segment.
Average sales per location for The Cheesecake Factory restaurants open for the full year were approximately $12.4 million for fiscal 2025.

Average sales per productive square foot (defined as all interior square footage plus seasonally adjusted exterior patio square footage) for restaurants open for the full year were approximately $1,151 for fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.claim: The Cheesecake Factory differentiates itself through a broad menu of approximately 225 items prepared from scratch daily and an average customer check of approximately $31.79 in fiscal 2025.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory menu features approximately 225 items, exclusive of beverage and dessert items and including items presented on supplemental menus, such as our SkinnyLicious® menu that offers innovative items at 590 calories or less.

In contrast to many restaurant chains, substantially all of our menu items, except those desserts produced at our bakery facilities, are prepared from scratch daily at our restaurants with high-quality, fresh ingredients using innovative and proprietary recipes.
The average check for each customer, including beverages and desserts, was approximately $31.79 during fiscal 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Vertically integrated bakery operations supply proprietary cheesecakes and desserts that generated approximately 17% of The Cheesecake Factory sales in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Integration of this vital part of our brand gives us control over the creativity and quality of our desserts and is also more profitable than buying from a third party.
Our brand identity and reputation for offering premium desserts results in a significant level of dessert sales, representing approximately 17% of The Cheesecake Factory sales during fiscal 2025.

LEVERAGING OUR DIFFERENTIATED POSITIONING TO DRIVE THE HIGHEST OFF-PREMISE AVERAGE WEEKLY SALES

competitive_position.claim: Experienced restaurant leadership supports execution, with General Managers and Executive Kitchen Managers averaging more than 15 years of company tenure (17 years and 16 years in the investor presentation) and Fortune naming the company to its "100 Best Companies to Work For®" list for 13 consecutive years through 2026.
quotes: Each restaurant is generally staffed with a General Manager (“GM”) and an Executive Kitchen Manager (“EKM”) who possess an average of more than 15 years of experience with the Company.
Fortune ‘100 Best Companies to Work For®’ List for 13 consecutive years
In 2026, we were named to the FORTUNE Magazine “100 Best Companies to Work For®” list for the thirteenth consecutive year.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 (landlord leverage stated as management belief)

We believe the relatively high sales productivity of our restaurants provides opportunities to obtain competitive leasing terms from landlords.

competitive_position.claim: In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, The Cheesecake Factory comparable restaurant sales grew 15.2% year-over-year as total revenues reached $1,033.4 million and income from operations rose to 74,873 (table in thousands) from 37,269 (table in thousands).
quotes: Total revenues were $1,033.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 compared to $907.2 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
The Cheesecake Factory restaurants led our performance, with comparable sales and traffic meaningfully outperforming the broader casual dining industry.

competitive_position.claim: Competitive performance has been uneven across concepts and periods: The Cheesecake Factory comparable sales grew 0.1% in fiscal 2025 due to a 2.3% customer traffic decline, while North Italia comparable sales fell approximately 2% in fiscal 2025 and (3)% in the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory comparable sales increased by 0.1%, or $2.2 million, from fiscal 2024.

The increase from fiscal 2024 was primarily driven by an increase in average check of 2.4% (based on an increase of 4.3% in menu pricing, partially offset by a 1.9% negative change from menu mix), partially offset by decreased customer traffic of 2.3%.
North Italia comparable sales decreased approximately 2% from fiscal 2024.

competitive_position.claim: The company faces intense direct and indirect competition for customer traffic, prime sites, and restaurant staff from full-service chains, independent restaurants, fast casual and quick-service concepts, grocery stores, and meal kits, including growing competition in off-premise channels.
quotes: We compete directly and indirectly for customer traffic with national and regional full-service dining restaurant chains as well as independently owned restaurants.

In addition, we face competition from fast casual and quick service restaurants, grocery stores and meal kits that have increased the quality and variety of their food products in response to consumer demand.

Growing competition in off-premise channels, our inability to differentiate our concepts in these channels or a change in customers’ willingness to pay fees associated with third-party delivery could negatively impact our comparable restaurant sales performance.
We also compete with other restaurants and retail establishments for quality sites and staff and managers to operate our restaurants.

competitive_position.claim: Labor, healthcare, commodity, and tariff-driven cost inflation poses an elevated threat because daily scratch preparation requires more restaurant-level labor than competitors using processed foods or commissaries, while menu price increases risk lowering customer traffic or shifting menu mix.
quotes: Increased restaurant labor costs could impact us more than others in our industry because we have a complex menu made fresh from scratch at our restaurants, requiring more labor at each restaurant location than some of our competitors who use processed foods or commissaries to prepare their foods.

However, our menu price increases may be insufficient to meaningfully offset increased costs and may, if not accepted by customers, result in reduced customer traffic and unfavorable menu mix shifts (i.e., customers reducing their spend by purchasing fewer menu items or lower cost menu items)

competitive_position.claim: Brand reputation is vulnerable to food-borne illness and contamination risks heightened by fresh in-restaurant preparation and third-party delivery, rapid amplification on social media, and reliance on company bakery facilities as the sole source for most baked desserts.
quotes: We freshly prepare our menu items at our restaurants, which may put us at greater risk for food-borne illness and food contamination outbreaks than some of our competitors who use processed foods or commissaries to prepare their food.

In addition to selling products throughout the world through various distribution channels, including, without limitation, supermarkets, mass market retailers, club stores and various other food service and retail channels, our bakery facilities are the only sources of most of our baked desserts to our restaurants.
These concerns are exacerbated by the speed with which negative information can be disseminated through social media.

competitive_position.claim: Expanding newer concepts—North Italia, Flower Child, and Other FRC—carries heightened execution risk, with no assurance of market acceptance or achieving targeted returns on new locations.
quotes: However, there is an enhanced level of risk and uncertainty related to the operation and expansion of our less-established restaurant concepts.

While we actively seek to grow these concepts, we can provide no assurance that new restaurants will be accepted in the markets targeted for expansion or that we will be able to achieve our targeted returns when opening new locations.

competitive_position.claim: Shifting consumer dining preferences—including potential effects from GLP-1 agonist medical treatments—alongside nutritional disclosure, ingredient, labor, and immigration regulations threaten market share and compliance costs.
quotes: New and current medical treatments such as GLP-1 agonists may shift consumer preferences.

Our failure to quickly and effectively adapt to any significant shift in consumer dining preference could cause our or our licensees’ restaurants to lose market share, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.

competitive_position.claim: Workforce or construction unionization attempts, macroeconomic pressures on consumer discretionary spending, adverse weather, public health emergencies, and acts of violence at restaurant centers are additional threats to traffic, expansion costs, and operations.
quotes: Our staff members and others may attempt to unionize our workforce, establish boycotts or picket lines or interrupt our supply chains, which could limit our ability to manage our workforce effectively, cause disruptions to our operations and could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Further, the unionization of construction companies could cause our construction and build-out costs for new restaurants to materially increase.

Any factor affecting consumer discretionary spending may influence customer traffic in our restaurants and average check amount, thus potentially having a material impact on our financial performance.

growth_thesis.claim: New restaurant openings are a primary driver of revenue growth, with 25 restaurants opened in fiscal 2025 and as many as 26 new restaurants expected in fiscal 2026.
quotes: Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.
Revenues increased 4.7% to $3,751.8 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $3,581.7 million for fiscal 2024, primarily due to additional revenue related to new restaurant openings.

We opened 25 restaurants in fiscal 2025 comprised of four The Cheesecake Factory, six North Italia, nine Other FRC and six Flower Child locations compared to 23 restaurants in fiscal 2024 comprised of three The Cheesecake Factory, six North Italia, eight Other FRC and six Flower Child locations.

The Company continues to expect to open as many as 26 new restaurants in fiscal 2026, including as many as five The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, eight North Italia locations, seven Flower Child locations and as many as six FRC restaurants.

growth_thesis.claim: Management targets 7% annual aggregate unit growth across concepts over the longer term, including a domestic target of approximately 300 Company-owned The Cheesecake Factory locations compared with 218 existing locations.
quotes: Longer-term, we believe our domestic revenue growth (comprised of our targeted annual unit growth of 7% in aggregate across concepts and comparable sales growth) combined with margin expansion, planned debt repayments and an anticipated capital return program will support our long-term financial objective of 10% to 15% total return to shareholders, on average.
We continue to target approximately 300 Company-owned and operated The Cheesecake Factory restaurants domestically over time.

We currently own and operate 384 restaurants throughout the United States and Canada under brands including The Cheesecake Factory® (218 locations), North Italia® (53 locations), Flower Child® (47 locations) and additional brands within our FRC portfolio (60 locations).

growth_thesis.claim: Continued unit expansion depends on finding sites that meet selection criteria, negotiating acceptable lease terms, obtaining permits, completing construction, and recruiting and training staff without macroeconomic or supply-chain delays.
quotes: In accordance with our broader capital allocation strategy, we plan to open as many locations in any given year as there are sites available that meet our site selection criteria and for which we can negotiate acceptable lease terms, obtain necessary permits, complete construction, and recruit and train personnel.

The development and opening process usually ranges from six to eighteen months, depending largely on the type and availability of the leased space we intend to occupy, our preferred opening date, as well as our ability to obtain goods, materials, permits and adequate staffing, and a variety of other circumstances beyond our control.

The impact of ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic events, including evolving government policies and global trade and tariff dynamics, could lead to issues such as further wage inflation, product and services cost inflation, disruptions in the supply chain, staffing challenges, shifts in consumer behavior and delays in new restaurant openings.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in [P2], with recent comparable sales declines at North Italia shown in [P3] and [P6].
growth_thesis.claim: New unit growth also requires market acceptance and achievement of targeted returns, which carry enhanced uncertainty for North Italia, Flower Child, and other FRC concepts.
quotes: However, there is an enhanced level of risk and uncertainty related to the operation and expansion of our less-established restaurant concepts.

While we actively seek to grow these concepts, we can provide no assurance that new restaurants will be accepted in the markets targeted for expansion or that we will be able to achieve our targeted returns when opening new locations.

growth_thesis.claim: North Italia, Flower Child, and Other FRC provide faster revenue growth than the flagship brand, with fiscal 2025 sales increasing 15.5%, 27.8%, and 18.4%, respectively, compared with 1.0% at The Cheesecake Factory.
quotes: The Cheesecake Factory sales increased 1.0% to $2,688.8 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $2,661.6 million for fiscal 2024.
North Italia sales increased 15.5% to $345.9 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $299.6 million for fiscal 2024.
Flower Child sales increased 27.8% to $185.3 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $145.0 million for fiscal 2024.
Other FRC sales increased 18.4% to $355.1 million for fiscal 2025 compared to $300.0 million for fiscal 2024.
In addition, our FRC subsidiary serves as an incubator, innovating new food, dining and hospitality experiences to create differentiated, high-quality concepts.

growth_thesis.claim: Comparable restaurant sales are a primary revenue growth driver and accelerated at The Cheesecake Factory to 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 and 7.5% for the 39 weeks ended September 29, 2026, following 0.1% growth in fiscal 2025.
quotes: Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.
Comparable restaurant sales at The Cheesecake Factory restaurants increased 15.2% year-over-year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.
The Cheesecake Factory comparable sales increased by 0.1%, or $2.2 million, from fiscal 2024.

growth_thesis.claim: Management seeks to grow comparable sales by raising average check through biannual menu price updates alongside menu innovation, the Cheesecake Rewards program, and digital and social media engagement.
quotes: For The Cheesecake Factory concept, our strategy is to increase comparable restaurant sales by growing average check while maintaining customer traffic.

We generally update The Cheesecake Factory menus twice a year, and our philosophy is to use price increases to help offset key operating cost increases in a manner that supports both our margin and customer traffic objectives.

Continued menu innovation, our rewards program and significant engagement across social media contributed to the impressive sales growth, while year-over-year improvements in labor productivity and food efficiency supported strong profitability.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated directly in [P2] and supported by fiscal 2025 traffic metrics in [P3].
growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining comparable sales growth requires maintaining customer traffic and perceived value amid competition and consumer discretionary spending sensitivity, because menu price increases can reduce traffic or shift mix unfavorably.
quotes: We believe that many consumers remain focused on value and if our competitors promote and deliver a higher degree of perceived value, our customer traffic could suffer.

However, our menu price increases may be insufficient to meaningfully offset increased costs and may, if not accepted by customers, result in reduced customer traffic and unfavorable menu mix shifts (i.e., customers reducing their spend by purchasing fewer menu items or lower cost menu items)

Any factor affecting consumer discretionary spending may influence customer traffic in our restaurants and average check amount, thus potentially having a material impact on our financial performance.

growth_thesis.claim: Sustaining brand-driven sales and social engagement depends on protecting reputation, preventing food-borne illness or safety failures, and retaining experienced restaurant managers and staff.
quotes: Negative publicity directed at any of our brands, regardless of factual basis, such as relating to the quality of our restaurant food or consumer packaged goods, the quality and condition of our restaurant facilities, customer complaints or litigation alleging injury or food-borne illnesses, food tampering or contamination or poor health inspection scores, sanitary or other issues with respect to food processing by us or our suppliers, labor relations, any failure to comply with applicable regulations or standards, allegations of harassment or disparate treatment based upon race, gender, gender identity, national origin, religion or other class, allegations of sexual harassment, politically motivated accusations or other negative publicity could damage our reputation.
These concerns are exacerbated by the speed with which negative information can be disseminated through social media.

One of the most important aspects of delivering a consistent and dependable level of service is having a team of experienced managers who can successfully operate our high-volume, complex restaurants.

Sales through the off-premise channel comprised approximately 21% of our restaurant sales during both fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2024.
$2.9 million in off-premise sales per restaurant based on annualized 3Q26.

growth_thesis.claim: Maintaining off-premise sales requires continuing to differentiate the concepts, preserving third-party delivery brand execution, and customers remaining willing to pay third-party delivery fees.

growth_thesis.claim: International licensing of 35 The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, along with two integrated bakery facilities and consumer packaged goods royalty streams, adds revenue and margin leverage.

Our objective is to drive margin expansion over time by leveraging incremental sales to increase restaurant-level margins at The Cheesecake Factory concept, leveraging our bakery operations, international and consumer packaged goods royalty revenue streams and G&A expense, and optimizing our restaurant portfolio.

growth_thesis.claim: International and bakery growth depends on avoiding bakery product recalls or withdrawals, complying with international trade and regulatory laws, and maintaining foreign market acceptance and licensee health.
quotes: If any of our bakery products becomes subject to a product recall or market withdrawal, whether voluntary or involuntary, our costs to conduct such recall or market withdrawal could be significant, restaurant sales as well as third-party sales of bakery products could be negatively impacted and our reputation could be damaged, any of which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.

Our international business exposes us to additional laws and regulations, including antitrust and tax requirements, anti-boycott legislation, import/export and customs regulations and other international trade regulations, privacy laws, the USA Patriot Act and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act.
